title: Long-Term Care Subsidies
description: Provides means-tested subsidies for long-term care services by MOH-funded long-term care providers.
highlights: For home and community long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
For institutional long-term care services provided by MOH-funded providers: Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
Additional subsidies of up to 15% for Singapore Citizens born in or before 1969

sections.About this support:
**For home and community long-term care services (e.g. Day Care, Community Rehabilitation services, Home Nursing, Home Medical)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 80%
- Additional 15% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969

**For institutional long-term care services (e.g. Nursing Home)**

- Means-tested subsidies of up to 75%
- Additional 5% subsidies for Singapore Citizens born in and before 1969
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Monthly per capita household income (PCHI) of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value (AV) of less than or equal to $21,000 for households with no income)
- Receiving long-term care services from MOH-funded providers
sections.How to apply?: Persons who require long-term care services can approach their doctor at the hospital, polyclinic, or Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) for assistance in applying for admission to a subsidised long-term care service.
sections.Where to go: [Find nearest AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/about-us/aic-link-locations/)

title: Healthier SG
description: A national strategy focused on preventive care to empower individuals to take steps toward better health, with the support of their Healthier SG clinic and community partners.
highlights: Receive dedicated care from your preferred Healthier SG clinic
Prevent or manage chronic conditions and complications
Create your Health Plan with your family doctor
Receive healthcare and medication subsidies and benefits

sections.About this support:
Benefits after enrolment include:

- Fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation and subsequent annual Health Plan check-ins with your enrolled Healthier SG clinic
- Healthpoints (worth $20) via Healthy 365 app after the first Health Plan consultation
- One-off Healthpoints (worth $10) via Healthy 365 app upon completing both an in-person annual Health Plan check-in and viewing of Health Plan on HealthHub within the qualifying period of 1 July 2026 to 31 December 2029.
- Special subsidies for Healthier SG screening tests and vaccinations (for eligible Singapore Citizens)
- Healthier SG Chronic Tier subsidy at Healthier SG clinics for CHAS cardholders with high medication requirements (for selected chronic medications at prices comparable to polyclinic prices)
- Full MediSave coverage for treatment of chronic conditions listed under the Chronic Disease Management Programme (CDMP), up to the relevant MediSave withdrawal limit
sections.Who is this for?: Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents aged 40 years old and above to enrol with a Healthier SG clinic or polyclinic
sections.How to apply?:
**Self-enrol via HealthHub**

If you are eligible, you will be invited via SMS to enrol in Healthier SG. You can do so in three simple steps:

1. Use the HealthHub app, which can be downloaded from Google Play or Apple App Store.
2. Choose your preferred Healthier SG clinic from the [list of more than 1,000 Healthier SG clinics](https://gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg).
3. Book an appointment for your fully subsidised first Health Plan consultation.

For a detailed step-by-step guide on how to enrol, click [here](https://www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/guide/).

If you have not received an SMS invitation, you can:

1. Request one by submitting your details at https://go.gov.sg/healthiersg-sms-invite
2. Contact the MOH hotline at 6325 9220

**Enrol with caregiver's assistance**

You can grant your caregiver/family member/loved one access to your HealthHub, so they can use their smartphone to help you enrol in Healthier SG. Follow the step-by-step guide at these links:

- [Grant your caregiver/family member access](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/addcaregiver/)
- [Assist your family member’s enrolment](https://safe.menlosecurity.com/https:/www.healthiersg.gov.sg/enrolment/caregivers/)

**Other assisted enrolment**

- Visit any ServiceSG Centre or AIC Link for enrolment assistance. To find an enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)
sections.Where to go: To find a Healthier SG clinic or enrolment station near you, visit [HealthierSGGoWhere](https://www.gowhere.gov.sg/healthiersg/)

title: Severe Disability Assessment (SDA)
description: Provides an assessment of your disability status conducted by a Ministry of Health (MOH)-accredited severe disability assessor.

sections.About this support:
SDA is required if you are:

- Applying for the following long-term care severe disability financial assistance schemes administered by the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC):
  - CareShield Life
  - ElderShield
  - ElderFund
  - Interim Disability Assistance Programme for the Elderly (IDAPE)
  - MediSave Care
- Applying for supplement schemes of CareShield Life and ElderShield administered by private insurers – Great Eastern, Income and SingLife
- Undergoing a disability review to ascertain continued scheme eligibility
- Undergoing an underwriting to enroll into selected schemes
sections.Who is this for?:
Anyone who require an SDA to determine your ability to perform each of the 6 Activities of Daily Living, as certified by an MOH-accredited severe disability assessor.

These 6 activities are:

- Feeding
- Dressing
- Toileting
- Washing
- Walking or moving around
- Transferring from bed to chair and vice versa
sections.How to apply?:
To find a severe disability assessors near you, you may visit the [AIC's website](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Severe-Disability-Assessment) and search using a postal code, address, or your device's current location.

If a service provider listed informs you that they do not conduct SDA, please [reach out to AIC with their details](mailto:apply@aic.sg).

For further assistance, you can contact AIC via the hotline[1800 650 6060](tel:18006506060).

- Airtime charges apply for mobile calls to 1800 service lines. Calls are free of charge only if made from regular land lines in Singapore.
- Calls from AIC Hotline may be reflected as 6650 6060 on your caller ID.

You can also visit the nearest [AIC Link](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)[ ](#_msocom_1)or [submit an enquiry](mailto:enquiries@aic.sg).
sections.What to expect?:
- **Assessments are strictly by appointment only**. Please call ahead to make an appointment with the clinic or assessor before going to the clinic.
- You will need to bring along relevant medical reports or discharge summaries related to your assessment when you go for your SDA appointment.
- If your care recipient requires a mental capacity assessment to be completed to obtain certification for the purpose of applying for AIC schemes, please explicitly request for it when making the appointment. Do note that mental capacity assessments can only be completed by doctors.
- A typical SDA will last about 45 minutes or longer.
- SDA fees are as follows, if:
  - You visit an assessor’s clinic: $100
  - An assessor visits your house: $250
- You will be reimbursed the assessment fee which you have paid if you are assessed to be severely disabled.
- For CareShield Life claims, the assessment fee for the first disability assessment will be waived, regardless of whether you are assessed to be severely disabled, or whether the claim is successful.

title: Caregivers Training Grant (CTG)
description: Subsidy for caregivers to offset the training fees of approved courses to equip themselves with the necessary skills to care for their loved ones.
highlights: $400 subsidy for the first year
$200 annual top-up, with a total CTG balance cap of $400 at any given time
Contact the service provider at least two weeks before the course starts

sections.About this support:
- $400 grant for eligible care recipients in their first year of tapping on CTG
- CTG balance can be used to subsidise their caregivers attending approved caregiver training courses
- Co-payment of at least $10 for every course attended by the caregiver
- $200 annual top-up in subsequent years, with total CTG balance capped at $400 at any given time
- If multiple caregivers of the same care recipient wish to attend training, they can tap on the same CTG balance available to offset the course fees
sections.Who is this for?:
Care recipient must be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- Aged 65 and older

OR

- Have a disability assessed by an approved healthcare practitioner

Caregiver must be:

- Main person caring for the care recipient (e.g. family members and foreign domestic workers)
sections.How to apply?:
- [Choose an approved course here](https://training-healthcare.vertis.digital/)
- Contact the training provider to confirm course details
- Register for the course
- Inform the trainer about using CTG at least two weeks before the course starts
- Your trainer will give you the CTG application form to fill out, and will submit it on your behalf
- [You can also visit the AIC’s website to download the CTG application form](https://www.aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Caregivers-Training-Grant)

sections.Phone number:
AIC Hotline: [1800 650 6060](tel:1800-650-6060)

title: Our Lives Our Voices (OLOV)
description: OLOV aims to empower clients to become self-advocates and foster an inclusive society where PWIDs can independently participate in the community in a meaningful manner. Through personalised training and peer support, it builds confidence and independence.

sections.About this support: The programme provides structured, personalised training supported by a customised web application, peer-led facilitation, and community engagement. It equips PWIDs with essential communication and interpersonal skills, empowering them to discover their strengths, express their views, take on meaningful community roles, and pursue greater autonomy, purpose, and active participation in society.
sections.Who is this for?:
1. PWIDs aged 18 years and above with an IQ below 70
2. PWIDs who demonstrate ability to participate in group training sessions, express basic intentions and preferences.
3. PWIDs registered under MINDS programmes
sections.How to apply?:
Interested applicants can apply through the following:

1. Email to [olov@minds.org.sg](mailto:olov@minds.org.sg)

2.  Submit the form via https://tinyurl.com/olovinterest

3. Call 65478503
sections.What to expect?:
1. Basic screening will be conducted to ensure that PWIDs meet the criteria
2. PWIDs will also be assessed over 2 trial sessions to determine suitability and interest.
3. Enrollment is throughout the year.

title: Migrant Domestic Worker Levy Concession
description: Provides concessionary levy at $60 per month if there is an eligible person residing in the household.
highlights: Concessionary rate of $60 per month, compared to standard levy of $300 for 1st MDW and $450 for subsequent MDWs
Each household is eligible for one MDW levy concession per eligible person, up to two MDW levy concessions per household

sections.About this support:
- Pay a lower levy of $60 per month if you live with an eligible person
- Levy concession can only be granted for one MDW per eligible person and is capped at two levy concessions per household
sections.Who is this for?:
If you live with any of the following eligible person who is a Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident:

- Child below 16 years old
- Elderly person who is at least 67 years old
- Person with disabilities (PWD) who must be certified by Singapore-registered doctor or an approved healthcare professional to permanently require some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
  - Washing
  - Dressing
  - Feeding
  - Toileting
  - Walking or moving around
  - Transferring
sections.How to apply?:
Before hiring an MDW, you are required to obtain an approval from the [Ministry of Manpower (MOM)](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/eligibility-and-requirements/employer-requirements) to hire an MDW.

If the eligible person is a PWD, you will also need to apply for the scheme:

- Online at the [AIC eServices for Financing Schemes (eFASS)](https://efinance.aic.sg/)

- At any of the [AIC Links](https://www.aic.sg/Contact-Us#map)

No application for the scheme is further needed if:

- You or your spouse is at least 67 years old
- Your child is below 16 years old

The levy concession will automatically start once you meet the eligibility criteria and complete the required steps listed on [MOM’s website](https://www.mom.gov.sg/passes-and-permits/work-permit-for-foreign-domestic-worker/foreign-domestic-worker-levy/levy-concession).

- Provides up to $250 cash payout per month for as long as they remain eligible

description: For persons with permanent disabilities who are medically certified as unable to take public transport and totally dependent on taxi for travel to school, work or SG Enable-supported training.

sections.About this support:
Persons with disabilities can apply for the means-tested subsidy for taxi travel for the purpose of school, work or employment-related training supported by SG Enable. The approved subsidy percentage* applies to the total fare for each trip (which covers additional charges such as booking fees, peak period surcharges and ERP charges).

The subsidy amounts will depend on:

- Whether applicants are Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Per capita monthly household income (PCHI)

* subjected to means testing and meeting eligibility criteria
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:

  - Autism

description: Subsidises the rental of essential care equipment for patients with serious illnesses.
highlights: Subsidised weekly rental fees for essential medical equipment
Covers up to two-way transport and essential consumables

sections.About this support:
The Equipment Rental Scheme (ERS) provides patients with serious illnesses who have a prognosis of less than a year with the following subsidies:

- Weekly rental fees for approved equipment such as wheelchair/pushchair, hospital bed, oxygen concentrator, pressure relief mattress and commode
- Cost of two-way transport for delivery and collection of rented equipment
sections.Who is this for?:

- Currently receiving care from a palliative care provider, whether home-based or in a public healthcare institution (PHI).
- Diagnosed to have a serious illness with a prognosis of less than a year.
- Assessed by a qualified assessor on the type(s) of equipment required.
- *Must not be receiving subsidies for the same or similar equipment through other Government assistance schemes.

*If you have previously received Government assistance or subsidies for same or similar type of equipment prior to your ERS application, eligibility to rent equipment(s) under ERS will be assessed on a case-by-case basis.

description: Community-based facilities that provide care and skills training to persons with disabilities aged 18 and above to maximise their independence.

- The DACs' programme is designed to equip persons with disabilities with daily living skills and community living skills to maximise their independence.

title: Assisted Deputyship Application Programme (ADAP)
description: ADAP supports caregivers of children without mental capacity to apply to be court-appointed deputies, through the simplified deputyship process. As a deputy, the caregiver can make legal decisions for the child when he/she turns 21.
highlights: Guidance provided for simplified deputyship applications for caregivers of persons with disabilities and without mental capacity
Acceptance of mental capacity assessment reports from SPED Schools, DACs, SWs, or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency

sections.About this support:
- Programme provides guidance/facilitation, for caregivers of persons with no mental capacity to manage their own matters in adulthood, to apply to Family Justice Courts to be appointed as legal deputies for their child. This is a simplified process that is also more affordable, compared to application for deputyship under standard route.
- Courts may accept mental capacity assessment reports prepared by psychologists from Special Education Schools (SPED Schools), selected Day Activity Centres (DACs), Sheltered Workshops (SWs), or the MSF-appointed ADAP Agency in lieu of a medical report. This applies only when the child is enrolled in a SPED school, DAC, or SW that is onboard the ADAP programme. In all other cases, the mental capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical capacity assessment must be conducted by a medical doctor or psychiatrist.
sections.Who is this for?:

  - above 18 years old and enrolled in an MSF-funded Day Activity Centre (DAC) or Sheltered Workshop (SW).
- You agree to use the standard list of powers/orders available under the Integrated Family Application Management System (iFAMS) when filing a simplified Deputyship application.
- All family members and any other caregivers agree for you to make the application (i.e. it is an uncontested case).
sections.How to apply?:
Caregivers can approach the relevant staff in the SPED school, Day Activity Centre or Sheltered Workshop to indicate interest to apply for Deputyship. The school or centre will work with an MSF-appointed ADAP Agency to guide the parent/caregiver in their Deputyship application.

title: Early Intervention Programme for Infants & Children (EIPIC)
description: EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0-6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

sections.About this support:
EIPIC is a centre-based programme that provides therapy and educational intervention for children aged 0 to 6 years who require medium to high levels of early intervention (EI) support.

The continuum of EI services include:

- EIPIC Under-2s
  - Targeted at children under 2 years old
  - Trains parents/caregivers so that they can effectively carry out intervention strategies in the child’s daily routines at home
- EIPIC@Centre
  - Provides both therapy and educational intervention services, typically in small groups
- DS-Plus
  - Provided in preschools targeted at children aged 2 to 6 years requiring low levels of EI support, and are attending preschools.
sections.Who is this for?:
Children who are:

- From birth to 6 years old
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents;
- Assessed by a paediatrician to be at risk of a developmental, intellectual, sensory or physical disability, or a combination of disabilities; and
- Not concurrently enrolled in any other ECDA-funded EI programmes (i.e. DS-LS, DS-Plus programmes).
sections.How to apply?:
- You may approach a doctor at any polyclinic to obtain referral for assessment at the Department of Child Development (DCD) at KK Women’s and Children’s Hospital (KKH) or Child Development Unit (CDU) at National University Hospital (NUH).
- Alternatively, you may approach a private paediatrician for assessment and recommendation for EIPIC.
- If your child is assessed to be suitable for EIPIC, the hospital or the private paediatrician will recommend EIPIC and submit the application to SG Enable upon your consent.

More information can be found on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/therapy-intervention/early-intervention-programme-for-infants-children).
sections.What to expect?:
- Upon receiving the referral, SG Enable will contact you within 10 working days to provide necessary information to help you make an informed decision on your choice of EI Centre.
- Your selected EI Centre will contact you within 2 weeks of referral to arrange an interview and assessment of your child.
- Enrolment into a suitable programme at the preferred centre is subject to the availability of vacancies at the centre and approval of the respective centre management.

sections.About this support:

- Group and individual activities to slow down deterioration of physical and mental functions (based on their abilities)
- Individualised care plans for seniors with suitable maintenance exercises
- Assistance with daily personal care
- Caregiver support activities (e.g. support groups, talks and care demonstrations, etc)
- Offered on weekdays, but some centres also provide weekend support

sections.About this support:

These services aim to better match persons with disabilities to jobs in the region based on their skills and interests and support them in employment.

EBH@Jurong

Located beside Lakeside MRT, at 111A Yuan Ching Road, Singapore 619606, EBH@Jurong aims to bring training and employment opportunities closer to the homes of persons with disabilities living in the West, including those with higher work support needs.

Key Features of EBH@Jurong

1. Provide targeted training and support** **to prepare persons with disabilities for employment in the logistics sector.
2. Provide on-site employment support, including longer and more intensive employment support for persons with disabilities with higher work support needs and require a longer runway of support to work independently in the community.

  - Intellectual disability

description: Enables parents to set aside CPF savings for the long-term care of children with special needs.

sections.About this support:
- Parents may nominate child with special needs to receive payouts from their CPF savings after death with minimum monthly payout of $250.
- If the nominating parent’s CPF savings upon his/her demise is insufficient to support a year’s worth of payout (e.g. a minimum monthly payout is S$250 x 12 months = S$3,000), the CPF savings will be disbursed as a lump sum to the nominee with special needs.
sections.Who is this for?:
The nominating applicant should be:

- Singapore Citizen or Permanent Resident
- The parent or an appointed legal guardian of the child with special needs

The child with special needs should:

- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

**Or**

- is attending or had attended a Special Education School

The 6 ADLs are:

- Eating
- Bathing
- Dressing
- Transferring
- Toileting
- Walking or moving around
sections.How to apply?:
Before proceeding, all applicants are encouraged to check if your child’s disability status has already been verified.

Find out more here: https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification

You can apply by submitting the completed [application form](https://www.sgenable.sg/snss) and supporting documents:

- via mail to Special Needs Savings Scheme (SNSS), Future Care Planning Resource Centre by SG Enable, 22 Lengkok Bahru, Vista, Enabling Village #03-03  Singapore 159824
- via email to [futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg](mailto:futurecareplanning@sgenable.sg).

You'll need to provide copies of:

- Nominating applicant's and child's NRIC

title: Gift Of A Lifetime Plus (GOAL+)
description: Gift Of A Lifetime Plus (GOAL+) aims to provide eligible caregivers of person with disability (PWDs) with an initial capital of $5,000 to set up trust accounts with Special Needs Trust Company Pte Ltd (SNTC). Under GOAL+, the Government sponsors matching donations of up to $10,000 for low- and middle-income families who contribute to the trust account within a five-year window period.
highlights: GOAL+ is a sponsorship scheme that aims to help caregivers save and provide for their dependant with disability. SG Enable Case Managers will invite eligible caregivers to apply for GOAL+ during the trust set-up process.

sections.About this support:
How does GOAL+ work?

1. GOAL+ runs from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031. Eligible caregivers whose PWDs do not have a Special Needs Trust (SNT) account can receive $5,000 from Community Chest to set up one.
2. Eligible caregivers of PWDs with verified disability can qualify for matching top-ups of up to $10,000 from the Government.
3. GOAL+ allows for a five-year top-up window for eligible SNT accounts, so that caregivers can plan contributions via cash top-up to the trust account in a more sustainable manner. Applicants are strongly encouraged to top up the trust account as soon as practicable. Any contribution made beyond the five years will not be entitled to matching top-ups from the Government.

title: Special Needs Trust
description:
Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC) is a not-for-profit trust company and a registered charity. As a fully owned subsidiary of SG Enable, SNTC provides affordable trust services to safeguard monies set aside by caregivers to fund the long-term care needs of their beneficiaries who are persons with disability. 

The Special Needs Trust (SNT) is a legal arrangement for SNTC to hold monies for persons with disability (PWD).
highlights: Sponsorship schemes eg GOAL+ are available to enable lower-income families set up the Special Needs Trust with $5,000.

sections.About this support:
After the Special Needs Trust (SNT) is set up, SNTC works with caregivers to put in place proper plans and arrangements that will enhance the financial well-being of PWDs (Beneficiary).

The SNT pathway is as per the following:

1. Caregiver opens an SNT account with an initial deposit of 5,000
2. Beneficiary receives gifts under the caregiver’s will, CPF cash and insurance nominations

Disburse funds to the beneficiary upon the caregiver’s passing or incapacity according to latter’s wishes set out in the Letter of Intent.

1. The trust fund is managed by the Public Trustee and principal value is guaranteed by the Government. SNTC fees are 90-100% subsidised by the Ministry of Social and Family Development.
2. Reviews are conducted periodically to check on the beneficiary's well-being.
3. Case Managers will advise caregiver on the future care needs of the beneficiary through a personalised care plan.
sections.Who is this for?:
Caregivers (Settlor) setting up the SNT should be:

- 21 years and above
- Has mental capacity
- Not an undischarged bankrupt

Persons with Disability (Beneficiary) must be:

- A Singaporean or Permanent Resident
- Residing in Singapore
- Has a verified disability

The CAREbuddy supports the Caregiver to work through personal and family goals, in ways that bring about positive changes.

Caregivers will be paired with a CAREbuddy who shares a similar profile, based on availability.

The dates and timing of the meet ups will be arranged according to both the CAREbuddy’s and Caregiver’s convenience.

CAREbuddy volunteers understand the challenges and experiences of caring for dependents with special needs or disabilities, as they are caregiver themselves.

sections.About this support:
The Enabled Living Programme (ELP) is a community living initiative that empowers adults with disabilities with low to moderate support needs to live independently for as long as possible.

Sited in public rental flats, ELP helps adults with disabilities age in place by providing an ecosystem of care and social support that includes on-site services – such as daily living and social skills coaching and community engagement.

By fostering community integration, ELP supports adults with disabilities to build meaningful connections, enhancing their overall well-being, autonomy, and dignity.

The ELP sites and appointed service providers are listed on the [Enabling Guide](https://www.enablingguide.sg/elp-and-hsp).
sections.Who is this for?:
Applicants should:

1. Be a Singapore Citizen​
2. Be aged 35 to 64
3. Have a permanent disability based on one or more the following [(refer to the disability profile(s) that each ELP site serves)](https://www.enablingguide.sg/im-looking-for-disability-support/child-adult-care/elp-and-hsp#abouttheelpsites):
  - Physical disability – Requires assistance with at least one of the six Activities of Daily Living (ADLs)* due to physical impairment
  - Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification)**  completed by a relevant registered Healthcare Professional.

1. Not be enrolled in any government-funded adult disability hostel, adult disability residential home or day activity centres
2. Not have any caregivers who are available or capable of caring for them
3. Not have significant physical health, mental health or behavioural needs that are beyond what ELP can reasonably support
4. Fulfils Housing and Development Board (HDB)’s public rental flat criteria under the Joint Singles Scheme

Applicants who do not meet the eligibility criteria may still be considered, subject to a case-by-case assessment.

Notes:

* The six ADLs are washing, dressing, feeding, toileting, mobility and transferring.

** From 8 September 2025, the Disability Verification Form (DVF) is the standardised proof of disability required to verify an individual’s disability status when applying for selected MSF disability schemes and services and other selected Government disability schemes. Applicants can check if their disability status is already verified via their Touchpoints, SupportGoWhere, or call SG Enable at 1800-8585-885.

title: Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund
description: Provides subsidies to seniors for mobility and assistive devices or home healthcare items.
highlights: Up to 90% subsidy for mobility and assistive devices (e.g. wheelchairs, hearing aids)
Up to 80% subsidies for home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, adult diapers)
Approach your therapist or AIC directly to apply

sections.About this support:
To support ageing in place, you may apply for the following subsidies for seniors who live at home:

- Subsidies of up to 90% for approved mobility and assistive devices (e.g. mobility aids such as walking/quad stick, wheelchair, geriatric chair, commodes, pressure relief mattress/cushions, hospital beds, spectacles, hearing aids, etc.)
- Subsidies of up to 80% for approved home healthcare items (e.g. milk feeds, diapers, etc.)
sections.Who is this for?:
- 60 years old and above
- Singapore Citizen or PR
- Monthly household income per capita of less than or equal to $4,800 (or property annual value of $21,000 or below for households with no income)
- Pass a [means-test](https://aic.sg/Financial-Assistance/Seniors-Mobility-and-Enabling-Fund---Mobility-and-Assistive-Devices#faq) for Intermediate and Long-Term Care (ILTC) services
- Seniors and persons with disabilities will be served under one scheme and agency throughout their lifetime
- If the individual has tapped on Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)^ before the age of 60, they will continue to be served by ATF throughout their lifetime and not SMF
- If the individual has not tapped on ATF subsidies before the age of 60, they would be served by SMF throughout their lifetime
- Individuals can approach their care provider, e.g. hospitals, community care organisations, social service agencies, to enquire about their eligibility for the schemes
- They may also approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) if they are not currently receiving support from any care provider

^ATF provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase the assistive technology devices to enable independent living

Additional criteria for assistive devices:

- Assessed by a qualified assessor to require the device
- Must not reside in a nursing home or sheltered home

Additional criteria for motorised devices:

- Must not have a full-time caregiver or domestic worker
- Unable to use a manual wheelchair independently
- Assessed to be mentally and physically able to safely use the motorised device

Additional criteria for home healthcare items:

- Must not be a current recipient of subsidies for the same items
- Must be receiving Home Nursing, Home Medical, Home Palliative Care, or Day Hospice services
sections.How to apply?:
You can apply:

- via the therapist or social worker at the hospital, day rehabilitation centre, or senior care centre from which your loved one is receiving care
- online [using Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-using-singpass) or [without Singpass](https://for.sg/smf-application-not-using-singpass)
- By mailing the [completed application form for assistive device or mobility device](http://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/SMF-Application-Form.pdf) and supporting documents to Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF), No. 7 Maxwell Road #04-01, MND Complex Annex B, Singapore 069111

You'll need to provide:

- Copy of Applicant's NRIC (front and back) or a copy of the digital NRIC available on SingPass
- For first time application for motorised device, doctor memo or [Need for Assessment form](https://edge.sitecorecloud.io/agencyforinb6cc-agencyforin73f5-production08ac-d178/media/agency-for-integrated-care/Files/Financial-Assistance/Cerification-of-Medical-Need-Form.pdf) indicating need for motorised device must be submitted.
- Copies of medical reports, if available
- Copies of financial assistance documents, if available

sections.About this support:

- The matching grant will automatically be credited to the MA of the eligible member at the beginning of the following year, i.e. from 2027

- Eligible beneficiaries will enjoy interest rates of up to 6% per annum on the cash top-ups and matching grant

- Cash top-ups that attract the Matched MediSave Scheme matching grant will not qualify for tax relief
sections.Who is this for?:

- Between 55 and 70 (inclusive) as of 31 December of the year
- Does not own more than 1 property

- Average monthly income not more than $4,000
- MA balance less than half the current Basic Healthcare Sum
sections.How to apply?:

title: Assistive Technology Fund (ATF)
description: Provides subsidies for persons with disabilities (PWDs) to purchase assistive technology devices to enable independent living. The devices should aid early intervention, education, training, employment, therapy, rehabilitation and/or independence in daily living for PWDs.
highlights: Subsidy of up to 90% of the cost of the required assistive technology device (lifetime cap of $40,000)
Apply through a therapist or social worker at public hospitals or social service agencies

sections.About this support:
- Subsidy of up to 90% of the cost of the required assistive technology device (lifetime cap of $40,000)
- Subsidy amount is determined according to the applicant's monthly household income
- Funds can be used to buy, replace, upgrade, or repair assistive technology devices
- The Fund does not support consumables. The Fund will cover medical devices (e.g. oxygen concentrators and suction pumps) and spectacles for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents at or above age 60, who remain served by ATF.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Singapore Citizens or Permanent Residents
- Have a permanent disability based on any one of the following:
  - Physical Disability: Requires some assistance with at least 1 of the 6 Activities of Daily Living due to physical impairment
  - A visual impairment: Moderate visual impairment or worse in the better eye
  - A hearing impairment: Moderate hearing loss or worse in the better ear
  - Intellectual disability
  - Autism

Proof of disability must be provided using the [Disability Verification Form](https://www.enablingguide.sg/disability-verification) completed by a relevant registered healthcare professional.

Undergone qualified assessor’s assessment to determine the need and type of device(s)

- Monthly Per Capita Household Income of $4,800 and below
- Annual Value (AV) of residence reflected on NRIC of $21,000 and below for households with no income

**Note for Singaporean and Permanent Resident Seniors:**

Subject to eligibility,

(a) Singaporean and Permanent Resident seniors who have not tapped on ATF before the age of 60 will be supported by the Seniors' Mobility and Enabling Fund (SMF). Please apply to SMF.

(b) Singaporean and Permanent Resident seniors who have tapped on ATF before the age of 60 will be supported by ATF throughout their lifetime.
sections.How to apply?:
- Approach a therapist or a social worker from public hospitals or social service agencies to assess and assist you to submit the application
  - If you are not currently under the care of any public hospitals or social service agencies, you may approach a polyclinic to obtain a referral letter to a public hospital for an assessment and thereafter submit the application.
- Before meeting your touchpoints, all applicants are encouraged to check if your disability status has already been verified by logging into [SupportGoWhere](https://supportgowhere.life.gov.sg/grants/pwdr/apply) with your Singpass. If you do not have a verified disability status, the touchpoint's registered healthcare professional will be able to guide you with the disability verification.
- Means testing is required and this will be assisted by the social worker at the public hospitals or social service agencies.

title: Settling Outstanding Tax Matters and Bills for a Deceased Person
description: Enables executors or administrators to settle the deceased's taxes and outstanding debts using the estate's funds before distribution to beneficiaries.
highlights: Settle the deceased's taxes and debts using the estate's funds

sections.About this support:
Executors or administrators of a deceased can act on the deceased’s following matters:

- Filing personal income tax for the deceased on the income earned up to the date of death.
- Filing estate or trust income tax for the deceased on the income. Estate income refers to the income generated by the deceased’s assets after date of death, during the administration of the estate. Trust income refers to the income from assets held in trust.
- Settling the taxes and other bills such as loans, funeral expenses and medical bills from the estate funds of the deceased before distribution to deceased’s beneficiaries.
sections.Who is this for?:
- Executors or administrators of a deceased’s estate who are responsible for settling outstanding taxes, debts and liabilities.
- Remember, the executor or administrator must ensure all outstanding taxes, loans, funeral expenses, and medical bills are paid from the deceased's estate before distributing the remaining assets to the beneficiaries.
sections.How to apply?:
File personal income tax for the deceased
Provide IRAS with the following details via [myTaxMail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/portal/correspondence/mytax-mail):
- Name, address and identification number of the legal personal representative who is handling the affairs of the deceased;
- Copy of the death certificate;
- Copy of the Grant of Probate/Letter of Administration, if available;
- Income details from all sources, up to the date of death (please specify the breakdown for each income source); and
- Type and amount of tax relief available/applicable to reduce the tax burden.
File an Income Tax Return for Estate or Trust Income
- Download and complete the Request Form for Form T from [IRAS's website](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/other-taxes/trusts/filing-estate-trust-income-tax-(form-t)/form-t).
- Email the completed form to [trust@iras.gov.sg ](mailto:trust@iras.gov.sg)and IRAS will provide you with:
  - a Trust Reference Number
  - a copy of Form T to complete
- Mail the completed Form T to this address: The Comptroller of Income Tax, 55 Newton Road, Singapore 307987.
sections.Where to go: 55 Newton Road, Revenue House, Singapore 307987
sections.Phone number:
For guidance, consult a lawyer or contact IRAS directly at [1800 356 8300](tel:1800-356-8300) or visit the IRAS office at 55 Newton Road, Revenue House, Singapore 307987, from Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm.  

If you need to speak with a tax officer, you are encouraged to [make an appointment](https://eappointment.iras.gov.sg/eappt/) at least 2 working days in advance.

[Incentives have ceased]

title: MediSave
description: A personal healthcare savings account that helps you pay for you and loved ones' healthcare expenses over your lifetime, especially when you retire and no longer have regular income.
highlights: Covers selected medical, treatment and hospital expenses, up to the approved limits
Covers for healthcare insurance premiums, rehabilitation and palliative care
Applicable at all MediSave accredited Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs)

sections.About this support:
- MediSave pays for a variety of medical expenses such as selected outpatient treatments, day surgery and hospitalisation expenses
- It also covers the costs for your rehabilitation and palliative care
- You can also tap on your MediSave to pay for health insurance premiums for yourself and your loved ones
sections.Who is this for?:
- You need to be a Singapore Citizen (SC) or Permanent Resident (PR)
- Your spouse, children and parents can be of any nationality, except grandparents and siblings who must be SC or PR
sections.How to apply?:
- To use your MediSave, inform the Public Healthcare Institutions (PHIs) or Medical Institutions (MIs) where you are receiving treatment at, and you would like to use your MediSave to pay for your medical expenses
  - If this is your first time applying, you will need to sign the Medical Claims Authorisation Form (MCAF)
  - If you had previously given a standing authorisation for the use of MediSave, the MI will submit a claim on your behalf
- The PHI and/or MI will submit the medical claim on your behalf and payment from your healthcare plans will be made directly to them
- Upon approval of the claim, the Board and/or insurer will notify you accordingly

title: Live Well, Age Well Programme
description: The Live Well, Age Well programme is co-organised by HPB and PA to provide holistic activities to improve the physical, mental and social health of adults aged 50 and above.
highlights: Discover free activities near you to stay healthy and active
Download the Healthy 365 mobile app on Apple Store / Google Play

sections.About this support:
- As we age, staying healthy and active is important so you can continue doing the activities you love.
- The Live Well, Age Well programme features a wide range of FREE^ exciting activities in your neighbourhood to help you kickstart your healthy living journey.
- Activities are specially designed based on the needs of adults aged 50 years old and above, so as to help you improve your physical, mental and social health to continue doing what you love.
- These programmes are available at multiple locations near you, including Community Centres/Clubs, Residents’ Committee, Residents’ Network Centres, Senior Activity Centres. Some programmes (e.g. group exercise sessions and workshops) are also available online, so you can stay healthy in the comfort of your home.

^Except for subsidised health screening programmes under Live Assured.
sections.Who is this for?:
- All Singapore residents aged 50 and above are welcome to join our Live Well, Age Well programme.
- There may be additional criteria for selected programmes.
- Visit [Live Well, Age Well website](https://www.healthhub.sg/programmes/160/AAP) for more information.
sections.How to apply?:
**Step 1**: Download the Healthy 365 mobile app on Apple Store / Google Play.

**Step 2**: Create profile if you are a new user. Log in to your existing profile with your NRIC and registered phone number if you are an existing user.

**Step 3**: Tap on "Explore" and select "Events" to view upcoming events.

**Step 4**: Search "Active Ageing" to filter for Live Well, Age Well programmes.

**Step 5**: Select the event you are interested in to view more details. Select "Book Now" to sign up.

You may also visit your nearest Community Clubs/Centres (CCs) or Residents’ Committees (RC)/Residents’ Network (RN) Centres for assistance.

title: Earned Income Relief
description: Provides tax relief for individuals who are gainfully employed or carrying on a trade, business, profession or vocation.
highlights: Provides tax relief of up to $12,000

sections.About this support:
- Receive tax relief of up to $8,000, depending on your age
- Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) are granted increased relief of up to $12,000
sections.Who is this for?:
- You are employed / self-employed and have received taxable earned income from your employment, pension or trade / business / profession / vocation in the previous year
- To be considered eligible for higher relief, PWDs must have a permanent disability or mental impairment affecting work ability defined as follows:
  - Physical disability - requires assistance in any of the following 6 Activities of Daily Living (ADLs):
    - Washing or Bathing
    - Dressing
    - Feeding
    - Toileting
    - Transferring
    - Mobility
  - Mental disability - impaired in any of the following 3 activities:
    - Self Care and ADLs
    - Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment
    - Education or Work
sections.How to apply?:
- The relief is granted automatically if you have taxable earned income
- If you are claiming Earned Income Relief (Disability) for the first time, please email the following via [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection):
  - Completed Tax Relief Form - [Application for Claim of Disability - Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
  - Letter / supporting documents from the disability association, indicating details of the disabilities
  - Next, you must complete your Income Tax Return as follows:
  - If e-Filing, enter disability or mental impairment details under Section "4. Deductions, Reliefs and Parenthood Tax Rebate" > "Earned Income Relief"
    - If using paper filing, include handicap details in Appendix 2 of the Income Tax Form
- Once claimed, the relief will be granted automatically in subsequent years if you are eligible

title: Qualifying Child Relief (QCR)/Child Relief (Disability)
description: Provides tax relief to parents to recognise their efforts in supporting their children.
highlights: Claim up to $7,500 per dependant
Can be applied alongside the Working Mother’s Child Relief (WMCR) scheme for additional support
Parents may share the QCR / Child Relief (Disability)

sections.About this support:
- QCR of $4,000 per qualifying child
- Child Relief (Disability) of $7,500 per child with disabilities
- Eligible working mothers can also apply for Working Mother's Child Relief (WMCR) in conjunction with the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) for additional support
- Parents may share the QCR / Child Relief (Disability) based on an agreed apportionment
sections.Who is this for?:
**To be eligible for QCR, you must meet all the following conditions:**

During the previous year,

- Your child is unmarried and is either:
  - Born to you and your spouse / ex-spouse
  - A stepchild
  - Legally adopted
- Your child was either:
  - Below 16 years old
  - Above 16 years old and studying full-time at any university, college or other educational institution
- Your child did not have an annual income exceeding $8,000.

**To be eligible for Child Relief (Disability):**

- Your child must be unmarried / have been unmarried in the previous year and is either:
  - Born to you and your spouse / ex-spouse
  - A stepchild
  - Legally adopted
- Your child meets any of the following criteria:
  - Your child is certified by a doctor to require assistance in any of the 6 Activities of Daily Living:
    - Washing or Bathing
    - Dressing
    - Feeding
    - Toileting
    - Transferring
    - Mobility
  - Your child is certified by a doctor to be impaired in any of these 3 areas:
    - Self-Care and Activities of Daily Living
    - Compliance to Psychiatric Treatment
    - Education or Work
  - Your child is attending (or is recommended by a doctor to attend) a Special Education (SPED) school
  - Your child is not attending a SPED school but has significant special educational needs, resulting in severe functional impairments

** **

**Conditions related to claiming WMCR together with QCR / Child Relief (Disability):**

- The total claimable relief for QCR, Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR combined is capped at $50,000 per child
- When claiming both QCR / Child Relief (Disability) and WMCR, the QCR and Child Relief (Disability) claims will take precedence. WMCR claims will only be applied after.
sections.How to apply?:
**Please refer to the following processes to apply for QCR:**

**For e-Filing**

- If claiming QCR for the first time, log in to [myTax Portal](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection) using your Singpass or [Singpass Foreign user Account (SFA)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/digital-services/others/singpass-foreign-user-account-(sfa)-for-foreign-individuals)
- Navigate to "Individuals" > "File Income Tax Return"
- Select "File" to File Income Tax Return
- Go to "4. Deductions, Tax Reliefs and Rebates"
- Select “Add New” > “Child".
- Fill in the relevant information and select “Update”.
- If you were previously approved for relief last year, the amount will be pre-filled and granted to you automatically this year
- If you would like to make changes, please follow the above e-Filing process for first-time applicants

**For paper filing**

- Complete the "Child Relief" section in Form B1 & B
- Include your child's details in Appendix 2 if it's your first time claiming

**Please refer to the following processes to apply for Child Relief (Disability):**

For first-time Child Relief (Disability) claims, email 1 of the following documents via [myTax Mail](https://mytax.iras.gov.sg/login/selection)

- Completed Tax Relief Form - [Application for Claim of Disability Related Tax Reliefs](https://www.iras.gov.sg/media/docs/default-source/uploadedfiles/application-for-claim-of-disability-related-tax-reliefs.doc?sfvrsn=442cf660_28)
- Letter / supporting documents from the disability association / SPED school in respect of your child, providing details of their disabilities, to IRAS

If your child is attending / has been recommended to attend a SPED school or has significant special education needs, please refer to the [“First-time Child Relief (Disability) claims” section on the Qualifying Child Relief (QCR)/Child Relief (Disability) page)](https://www.iras.gov.sg/taxes/individual-income-tax/basics-of-individual-income-tax/tax-reliefs-rebates-and-deductions/tax-reliefs/qualifying-child-relief-(qcr)-handicapped-child-relief-(hcr)) for more details.

title: Merdeka Generation Package
description: Supporting Merdeka Generation seniors in their silver years by helping them to stay active, healthy and providing peace of mind over future healthcare costs.
highlights: Provides various health-related benefits to support seniors’ ageing, such as additional Outpatient Care subsidies and additional MediShield (MSHL) premium subsidies

sections.About this support:
Provides the following benefits to support healthcare for Merdeka seniors:

Additional Outpatient Care Subsidies
Additional subsidies for outpatient care at polyclinics, public Specialist Outpatient Clinics and Community Health Assist Scheme clinics.
Additional MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
Provides an additional 5% subsidy for your annual premiums, increasing to 10% after turning 75 years old.
[Redemption has ended wef. 31 Dec 2023] 
$100 Passion Silver Card Top-Up
One-off $100 top-up for use on active ageing programmes, public transport, merchant benefits etc (redemption has ceased wef. 31 Dec 2023).
[Top-Up has ended] 
Annual MediSave top-ups of $200 (2019-2023)

MediSave can be used to cover hospitalisation and treatment costs, pay various medical-related premiums etc.

title: Car Park Label Scheme
description: Provides two types of labels that allow drivers (Class 1) and passengers (Class 2) with medically certified mobility challenges to park at accessible spaces, so they can board or alight from their vehicles safely.
highlights: Eligible drivers and passengers with mobility impairment can apply for a Car Park Label to use accessible lots

sections.About this support:
- Car park labels allow access to accessible lots for easier boarding and alighting for drivers and passengers with mobility impairment
- Each label can be used by the label holder only. Car park labels are not applicable to motorcycles
- Option for Social Service Agencies (SSAs) to obtain labels for vehicles providing dedicated transport to passengers with mobility impairment
sections.Who is this for?:
- For Class 1: Drivers who are certified by Singapore registered medical professionals to require the use of bulky mobility aids and need to open the vehicle doors fully to board or alight from the vehicle.

title: MediShield Life Premium Subsidies
description: To keep MediShield Life premiums affordable, the Government provides several premium support measures, such as Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies.
highlights: Premium subsidies of up to 60%
Pioneer and Merdeka Generation subsidies

sections.About this support:
**Eligibility criteria for Premium Subsidies:**

- Premium Subsidies of up to 60% for eligible lower-to middle-income households
- Pioneer Generation Subsidies of between 40-60%, depending on age
- Merdeka Generation Subsidies of between 5%-10%, depending on age

As of 1 Apr 2025,

Household Monthly Income Per Person
Subsidy Range (tiered by age)
$0 - $1,500
25% - 60%
> $1,501 - $2,600
20% - 55%
> $2,601 - $3,600
15% - 40%

Note: The above subsidy rates apply to those living in property with an AV of $21,000 or less. Properties with an AV between $21,001 and $31,000 receive 10% less subsidies. Permanent Residents (PRs) receive half the subsidy rate applicable to Singapore Citizens (SCs). Those who live in residences with an AV above $31,000 or own multiple properties will not receive these subsidies.

**Eligibility for Pioneer Generation Subsidies:**

- Applicable for Pioneers, regardless of their household monthly income or the AV of their residence

**Eligibility for Merdeka Generation Subsidies:**

- Applicable for Merdeka Generation seniors, regardless of their household monthly income or the AV of their residence, on top of the Premium Subsidies that the seniors may be eligible for

Please [click here](https://www.moh.gov.sg/healthcare-schemes-subsidies/medishield-life/medishield-life-premiums-and-subsidies) for more information on Premium Subsidies, Pioneer Generation Subsidies and Merdeka Generation Subsidies.
sections.Who is this for?:

- Household monthly income per person of $3,600 or below; and
- Living in property with an Annual Value (AV) of $31,000 and below; and
- Not owning more than 1 property
sections.How to apply?: The subsidies that you are eligible for will be automatically applied to your MediShield Life premiums.

Open to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents living overseas

sections.About this support: Covers MediShield Life and/or CareShield Life premiums (where applicable) for the next 2 policy years upon approval.

- If you are granted APS and purchase an Integrated Shield Plan and/or ElderShield/CareShield Life Supplement afterwards, you will stop receiving APS

- The invitation will include an application form with details on the application process, which must be submitted along with the relevant supporting documents
